title: Three ways electrons move
question: How can the huge number of organic reactions be sorted by how their electrons move?
hook: There are about a thousand named reactions, but only a few ways for electrons to move.
idea: Most organic reactions fall into polar, radical or pericyclic classes, depending on how their electrons move.

beats.prompt: Match each class of reaction to how its electrons behave.
pairs: Electron pairs move from a clear source to a clear sink
Bonds shift around a cyclic transition state
beats.explain: Polar, radical and pericyclic reactions are the mechanistic classes, told apart by how electrons move.

beats.prompt: Sort each item into reaction types or reagent examples.
beats.explain: Reaction types describe what happens to the molecule, while reagents are the substances, often inorganic, that a transformation requires.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Chemists often sort reactions by mechanistic class: polar, radical or pericyclic.
Every reaction therefore fits neatly into exactly one of the classes.
Polar reactions are the largest group, making up the vast majority.
Polar reactions move electron pairs from a source to a sink.
beats.explain: Some chemical processes involve steps from two or even all three classes, so the scheme is not always clear.

beats.prompt: In one reaction, bonds are redistributed around a cyclic transition state and electron pairs circle around without a true source or sink. What must hold for this to work?

choices.label: The orbitals of the participating atoms must overlap continuously
A strong acid must pass protons along throughout
choices.feedback: Acids are one type of reagent, but this reaction is defined by its cyclic electron movement.

choices.label: Free radicals must carry single electrons
choices.feedback: Single electrons moving belongs to radical reactions, not this one.

choices.label: A small molecule such as water must be split off
choices.feedback: Splitting off water describes condensation reactions, not this class.

beats.explain: Pericyclic reactions need continuous overlap of the participating orbitals and are governed by orbital symmetry.
